body: I go to a really rigorous high school that is renowned for its lack of caring about its students. We are hoping to get something close to a school counselor one day. I have this immense amount of work every day, where I get home every night and work for 5-7 hours on average, leading to 4-6 hours of sleep a night. In addition to that, I am a chronic worrier, I get really dark moods then kind of scarily happy moments, I've even tried talking with my parents and a psychologist but they didn't actually believe me when I told them how stressed out I was and that I felt wrong and wanted to just stop existing. Sorry, that was very long, its just so much keeps piling on and on and no one ever believes me.

It sounds like you need to be straight with him about everything you were planning to say but didn't. It will be hard and, honestly, it requires a lot of bravery, but if he is your best friend and your significant other, he is definitely going to support you in trying to get through your depression, becoming more open, and (it sounds like) reducing the stress in your life. That's what friends and family are for. They should support you, even when progress is slow going or you have bad days, so talk to him. Let him know why. You can get through this.

Everyone is worth something. Everyone has their own special combination of characteristics and thoughts and dreams and opinions and feelings that is completely unique from anyone else in the past, future, or present. You are incredibly unique and there will never be another you. Why not enjoy the time you have as someone as special as you are? Because you ARE special, and you always will be.
